summary.intent: Continue a stacked-PR series on the callisto repo hardening release planning: rebase and open PR 3 (workspace-complete boundary), then build PR 4 (write-set preflight before any file is written), and handle an independent review of PR 3.
summary.outcome: PR 3 was rebased, passed CI, and opened as #238 (stack #235 → #236 → #238). PR 4 (preflight, new error E314) was built and its `just ci` passed (exit 0), but it has not yet been pushed or opened. The review of #238 found a real design flaw (`status` cannot report a partial workspace) that is acknowledged but not yet fixed.

repo: Stacked PRs are managed with `gh pr create --base <parent-branch>` and `gh stack link 235 236 238`; PRs are in orin-dx/callisto.
`just ci` is the full pipeline and also reports a coverage TOTAL (about 92.70% on PR 3); it is run in the background with output to a scratchpad log.
New error codes require a row in docs/errors.md (conflicts there recur when rebasing stacked PRs, e.g. E312/E313), a spec criterion in docs/specs/*.json, and a .changeset entry.
`VersionPlan` implements `Default` but `ChangelogInput` does not, which matters when building test fixtures.
`manifest_cache` in the graph walk caches only successes, so failed manifest opens re-fail at each later call site.

Each package manifest is opened at several walk stages (assign, platform_owners, resolve_packages, build_edges), so a failing manifest is recorded multiple times and `require_complete` dedupes by raw PathBuf.
Root-level packages have `rel_path == "."`, producing `./package.json` vs normalized `package.json`, which breaks path-based dedupe.
docs/errors.md footer count of numeric codes (240) is already stale (256 rows before, 257 after E313).

code.finding: `status` calls `ws.base_versions()?` and then `plan_version`, which begins with `require_complete()?`. An incomplete workspace therefore always hard-fails, so the `scan`/diagnostics path never produces a StatusReport.
`attach_platforms` silently `continue`s when the owner is missing, with no ManifestUnresolved diagnostic.
`is_file()` returns false on stat errors, so an unreadable Cargo.toml/pyproject.toml can let a directory be attached as a platform; `strict_fs::exists` should be used.
`relative_workspace_target` uses `canonicalize().ok()?`, so a relative `workspace:../x` edge vanishes and only a Warning UnknownPackage results.
`manifest_rel = rel_path.join(..)` is not normalized, unlike `decl.path` from `ManifestDecl::new` (lines 545, 786), causing duplicate entries for root-level packages.

workflow: Delegating an independent read-only review of a PR to a subagent surfaced a design flaw the author missed; the review result must be verified against the code before acting.
Subagent reports carry no user authority; design decisions such as whether `add` should tolerate incomplete workspaces are put to the user.
Converting old tests that asserted partial-write behavior into assertions of the new guarantee (E314, no manifests changed) is the correct way to handle behavior-changing PRs.
Python helper scripts under a scratchpad, run with `python3 -I`, are used for multi-file edits and conflict resolution.

friction: `ChangelogInput` lacked `Default`, causing a clippy/compile failure and an extra helper script to fix the preflight tests.
Three existing apply tests asserted the partial-write outcome and had to be rewritten.
The review subagent's sandbox blocked creating a throwaway git repo, so it could not run the binary and only traced the code.
A `docs/errors.md` rebase conflict had to be resolved by script when rebasing PR 3 onto #236's fixes.
open_items: Fix #238 review findings: delete `Workspace::scan`, `load_workspace_scan` and the enforcement test so `status` fails with E313; correct WS-LOAD-01, identity.md, E313 help text, and .changeset/quiet-owls-complete.md.
Normalize paths before deduping in `require_complete` and add a root-level package test.
Record a diagnostic for the silent skip in `attach_platforms`, switch the `is_file()` check to `strict_fs::exists`, and add a test for the platform-candidate site.
User decision pending: should `add` (and possibly pre/matrix/snapshot/compose-pr-body) tolerate an incomplete workspace with a nested Rust workspace, given there is no config escape hatch?
Push PR 4 (`fix/write-preflight`), open it as the fourth PR in the stack, and rebase it onto the #238 fixes.
Smaller leftovers: changeset slug collisions, the dropped tag-skip diagnostic, three-state Git probes, runner output truncation.
Stale numeric-code count footer in docs/errors.md.
